rationale: E10's A1-BDT arm (H1) was NOT MET as scored, and every deviation traced to the arm's plan and its registered scorer, not to the verifier (drafts/round13/E10_RESULTS_NOTES.md): with trials 15 s apart and ages 15, 30 and 45 s, a later trial's forged row could land in the same or the neighbouring one-second segment as an earlier one; the registered row_outcome scored a trial as detected whenever its second was flagged, so a benign row in a second flagged by another trial's attributable row counted as detected; and the registered prediction ignored copy mode's observation window (a copy can capture a transaction still in flight). E10b re-runs the same arm on the same stack and monitors, spaced so that no two forged rows share or neighbour a second, and scores each trial from its own row, with the segment verdict as a consistency check. It is a confirmatory test of H1's stated boundary with the scorer fixed in advance; re-scoring E10's data with it is exploratory (the dry run in the basis file).

schedule_arithmetic.argument: start_j >= start_i + (j - i) * spacing (op_bdt waits for nxt = start + spacing); t_ins = start + delta; target = t_ins - age; so target_j - target_i >= (j - i) * spacing - delta_max - (age_j - age_i) >= 50 - 8 - 40 = 2 s, and a difference of 2 s or more puts the rows in seconds at least 2 apart (neither shared nor adjacent)

hypotheses.H1b_backdating_boundary_own_row: Per trial and monitor, the verdict on the trial's own forged row equals the outcome the E10b prediction rule gives from that monitor's own polls; every non-excluded trial whose prediction is not ambiguous agrees. Consequences per level (prediction_per_level): a row backdated by 5, 15 or 30 s is never attributable; 45 s is attributable in every trial; 33 s is attributable exactly in the trials in which the last poll lacking the row copied within the 3 s before the insertion.
hypotheses.H1b_seg_segment_consistency: For every non-excluded trial and monitor, the own row is attributable if and only if its one-second segment is flagged.
hypotheses.H1b_lb_lower_bound (secondary): For every trial whose prediction is a non-ambiguous late verdict, the verifier's committed_after_lower_bound_s of the own row equals the predicted lower bound (max copy_at over the polls lacking the row, minus the row's timestamp) within 10 microseconds.
hypotheses.H1b_late_view (secondary): Copy mode takes its view of the -wal late in the copy: for every non-excluded copy-mode trial, the own-row outcome equals the prediction obtained when a copy whose observation window overlaps the write holds the row if and only if the copy ended (its record ts) after t_insert; reported in particular for the trials the primary rule calls ambiguous.
hypotheses.H10b_clock_step_state_rows (secondary ar: With homeprov_e10b's clock_step_all (time.time and homeassistant.helpers.entity.timer stepped), the hub's state rows and event rows written during a 60 s backward step and stamped more than 5 s before the step began are excused_clock_step under an operator CLOCK_STEP marker and attributable without one; a 10 s step leaves no attributable row in the step's key range and no flagged second in [t_on - 11 s, t_off + 1 s].

prediction_rule.views: a poll lacks the forged row if its view of the recorder was taken before the insertion began (t_insert, the hub's time just before BEGIN IMMEDIATE), holds it if taken after COMMIT returned (t_commit), and may do either if the two overlap

observation_window.direct: [copy_at, copy_at]: the read transaction's snapshot is pinned by the first read right after copy_at (monitor.py direct_snapshot)
observation_window.copy: [copy_at, record ts]: copy_at is the copy's start; the copy reads the database file, then the -wal (where the trial's frames are), then the -shm, and the record's ts is taken right after; the WAL is read somewhere inside, and a copy can capture a transaction whose COMMIT has not returned yet (E10 DEL 69 investigation, exp/out/r16_e10_del69_overlap.json)
observation_window.ambiguous_s: both windows widened by 50 ms on each side (E10's registered ambiguous_s)

prediction_rule.evaluation: every split of the overlapping polls into a lacking prefix and a holding rest is evaluated as the verifier evaluates a late row (testbed/e10b/e10b_score.py _verdict_for, mirroring e7_verify.py Timeline, ObservationBreaks and the late-row test)

outcomes.no_evidence: the first poll covering the row's second (through >= second + 1) holds the row, or no poll covers it
outcomes.detected: max copy_at over the polls lacking the row, minus the row's timestamp, exceeds LATE_BOUND (30 s)
outcomes.unknown: otherwise, no valid poll holds the row, or an observation break (unobservable, missing or backlogged poll, monitor restart, more than GAP_S = 30 s between copies) lies between the last lacking and the first holding poll

prediction_rule.ambiguous: the splits give more than one outcome, or the lower bound lies within 1 ms of 30 s: counted, left out of agreement, observed outcome reported
prediction_rule.a_priori_bound: a poll lacking the row copied before t_commit + 50 ms, so the predicted lower bound is below age + (t_commit - t_insert) + 0.05 s: below 30 s at 5 and 15 s; at 30 s above 30 s only through a poll whose view overlaps the insertion's own write (ambiguous by construction)

prediction_per_level.5: never detected: reported_late, or no_evidence when no poll lacking the row covered its second (copied at or after second + 1 before the insertion); unknown only after an observation break
prediction_per_level.15: never detected: reported_late (no_evidence only if no poll copied in the 14 s before the insertion)
prediction_per_level.30: never detected: reported_late; ambiguous when a poll's view overlaps the insertion's write window
prediction_per_level.33: detected iff the last poll lacking the row copied after t_insert - 3 s (a priori about 3/T of trials, T the monitor's poll interval; not a hypothesis); ambiguous when a copy-mode poll that copied in those 3 s overlaps the write
prediction_per_level.45: detected in every trial (some poll lacking the row copied in the 15 s before the insertion), unless a monitor did not observe in those 15 s

exclusions: a trial the integration reports with err (no row, lock unavailable, no cover): listed, not scored

a pair of trials whose forged rows' seconds are equal or adjacent (realised from their own timestamps): both excluded from H1b and H1b-seg, listed (the schedule makes this impossible while delta <= 8 s)
a trial whose prediction is ambiguous: counted, left out of agreement, observed outcome reported
a monitor whose verification failed: H1b not evaluable for that monitor (listed)
a block during which the host log shows a wall-clock gap above 90 s, or a hub start without a harness cause, or a monitor restart: its trials are scored and reported separately, not pooled (as E10)
stopping_rules: a preflight failure (E10's frozen files or this registration's files changed, tests failing, image contents differing from the repository, plan sha256 differing) stops the run before any trial: no data
no interim look at any verdict; the run is never stopped for an outcome

an infrastructure failure (hub not writing, a monitor's seal not anchored within 5400 s, the bdt command not acknowledged within n * spacing + 1800 s, the SSD or Docker failing) leaves the run incomplete: reported as incomplete; at most one re-run under a new tag (e10b_main2), after an amendment registered and stamped before it starts; trials of an incomplete run are reported, never pooled with the re-run
a failure of A6-CS2 does not affect H1b (snap_bdt is taken before it); H10b is then not evaluable
analysis_plan: Both monitors are scored and reported separately; nothing is pooled across them

H1b is met for a monitor only if every non-excluded trial with a non-ambiguous prediction agrees; any disagreement is reported with its trial (never averaged away); detection per level with exact 95% Clopper-Pearson intervals; no other hypothesis test
H1b-seg is met for a monitor only if every non-excluded trial is consistent
The secondary and exploratory outcomes are reported as such; E10's frozen rule and outcome serve as comparison only
Every deviation from this registration (plan, parameters, code) is written to an amendment before it is used
known_limits_stated_in_advance: One scratch stack on one Mac with virtual devices (E10's configuration path: the lab configuration cloned read-only at run time, which may differ from E10's clone; E9's final recorder snapshot, sha256 recorded by e10_stack.sh); the hub and the monitors share Docker's VM clock

Background load differs from E10's: the lab installation's own containers (hpr-hass, hpr-monitor, hpr-anchord) were running during E10 and are stopped during E10b (stopped 2026-10-24 to free memory for another project's run; the preflight records the count of running hpr-* containers); the other projects' runs on this Mac ended before E10b (2026-10-26 02:07Z and 02:20Z, by their end messages) and nothing else is scheduled during it

HOMEPROV detects rewriting after the monitor sealed a segment; it does not prevent it: the forged rows stay in the recorder, and a row backdated by less than about 30 s plus the poll interval remains outside the guarantee by design (H1b tests that boundary, it does not move it)
Copy mode's observation instant is resolved only to the copy's duration ([copy_at, record ts]); trials whose outcome depends on where the WAL was read are ambiguous and not scored
The schedule assumes delta_i <= 8 s (time from a trial's start to its insertion); E10's upper bound is in the basis file; a realised violation is caught (exclusion), not prevented
The 33 s detection share depends on the poll timing of this run; only the per-trial prediction is a hypothesis

The clock step is emulated inside the hub's process (time.time and helpers.entity.timer), not a host clock step; helpers/event.py's time_tracker_timestamp (the scheduler's clock) is left unpatched on purpose; an integration binding time.time itself would keep real timestamps

homeprov_e10b is unit-tested offline against Home Assistant 2026.2.3 (the newest release this Mac's Python 3.13 can install); the scratch hub runs 2026.7.4, whose helpers/entity.py (timer = time.time, time_now = timer() passed to async_set_internal) and core.py (Event: time.time()) were read from its PyPI wheel; the smoke checks it at run time (manipulation check)
E10b runs after another project's long run on the same Mac; CPU contention would change poll intervals, which the prediction takes from the chain, not from an assumed interval
